partners.mechanism_chain: HNF4A (HGNC:4835) —DISRUPTS→ impaired insulin secretion (HP:0000824); HNF4A (HGNC:4835) —DISRUPTS→ insulin resistance (HP:0000845); impaired insulin secretion (HP:0000824) —LEADS_TO→ diabetes mellitus (HP:0005978); insulin resistance (HP:0000845) —LEADS_TO→ diabetes mellitus (HP:0005978); WT1 (HGNC:12408) —DISRUPTS→ podocyte differentiation (GO:0001870); podocyte differentiation (GO:0001870) —DISRUPTS→ glomerular filtration barrier integrity (HP:0030186); glomerular filtration barrier integrity (HP:0030186) —LEADS_TO→ nephropathy (HP:0000139). Mutations in HNF4A cause MODY1 by disrupting pancreatic beta-cell function, leading to impaired insulin secretion and insulin resistance, ultimately manifesting as diabetes mellitus. Mutations in WT1 cause Frasier syndrome by disrupting podocyte differentiation, leading to compromised glomerular filtration barrier integrity and nephropathy. Both HNF4A and WT1 play crucial roles in cellular differentiation and function, and their dysregulation converges on processes vital for kidney function and metabolic homeostasis.
